subject: Discovery call recap & next steps — rotating demo slots
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery call recap & next steps — rotating demo slots

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Primary use case: real-time customer support routing + summarization for high-volume chat sessions.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms p99 token latency for short responses, encryption-by-default, and strict data residency for EU customers.
- Primary stakeholders: you (Engineering lead), Priya (CTO), and procurement for contract discussions.

Next step: we recommended a technical deep dive / demo with a solutions engineer to validate latency and integration points (KV cache, streaming responses, and routing policies). Camila (cc'd) would lead the tech portion.

To make scheduling painless across your team (US/EU/APAC), suggested approach is a rotating set of weekly slots so the meeting times fairly alternate between regions and reduce burden on any one timezone. Proposed rotation (all sessions 45 min + 15 min buffer):

Option A (rotating weekly):
- Week A (EU-friendly): Tue 10:00 CET / 09:00 GMT / 01:00 PT
- Week B (US-friendly): Wed 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 18:00 GMT
- Week C (APAC-friendly): Thu 09:30 IST / 16:00 JST / 19:00 AEST

If that feels heavy, we can do a simpler alternating cadence (EU weeks / US weeks).

Please let me know which of the following you prefer: 1) commit to rotating weekly schedule above, 2) alternate EU/US weeks only, or 3) propose specific recurring slot(s) that work for your team. If you like, you can pick times directly via our Calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo-30

Attached a short demo agenda and an SLA draft for context.

Thanks — looking forward to locking in a time.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: DemoAgenda.xlsx, SLA_Draft_v1.pdf

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the clear options. A few constraints from our side:
- Priya and I prefer mornings CET (09:00–11:30 CET) or late afternoons PT (16:00–18:30 PT) for cross-team attendance.
- Weekdays are best; Fridays are tough for our engineers.
- We have recurring sprint meetings Tue mornings US time, so Tuesday US mornings are not ideal.

Given that, I think an alternating EU/US cadence is the most realistic for us (Option 2). For next week, our availability windows:
- Tue 10:00–11:00 CET (works for Priya)
- Wed 16:30–17:30 PT (I can make this if needed, but Priya would be late)

If you can propose a concrete slot for Week A (EU) that falls in Tue 10:00 CET, we'll try to confirm. Also prefer Google Meet links rather than Zoom.

Thanks — Alex

Plan (every other week alternating):
- EU Week (Week A): Tue 10:00 CET / 09:00 GMT / 01:00 PT — 45 min technical deep dive (Camila leads) + 15 min buffer
- US Week (Week B): Wed 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET — same format

For next week (EU week), I'm tentatively holding: Tue, 10:00 CET (Tue 01:00 PT) — I realize that's early for the US; if that works for Priya and team, Camila will do a recorded portion for anyone who can't attend live. If Tue 10:00 CET is confirmed, we'll send a Google Meet invite and include a short agenda focused on integration points, performance targets (p99 token latency), and a live run of a sample integration.

If Tue 10:00 CET is tight, alternate EU options I can offer: Tue 09:00 CET or Wed 11:00 CET.

I'll also add a recurring slot to our Calendly for you and Priya to pick a time if that ends up being easier: https://calendly.com/redwood/demo-30

Let me know which of the two you want to lock — Tue 10:00 CET or Tue 09:00 CET (both next week).

Best,
Marissa
